intro: Basic code for talking to the SDK: send a request and continue from its reply, listen to events the SDK pushes, handle errors, never wait without a limit. The code is the GettingStarted code (Swift, Kotlin) and the Flutter app code, trimmed to the SDK calls; files marked ADDITION are ours.

addDelegate and receive: warning, runtime error (SDK restarts itself afterwards), fatal error, invalid state.

rules: Never pass nil as completion handler for an event with a result event (Start, Restart, Activate, OfflineLogin, ...): the result comes only through the handler. nil is for events whose result is none or Acknowledge; see completion_handler.

Debug on the console: print every completion handler and every delegate callback (name, status, error domain/code/description; URLs without query; never codes, tokens, passwords). A blank WebView or a silent step is then visible in the Xcode console / GetConsoleOutput. Register KsTrustedWebView.setLogListener too; onURLBlocked is the usual reason for a blank page.

Trusted WebView: never load a bare authorisation URL. Send GetAstClientData first, put code_challenge/code_challenge_method (from the result) into the URL and the headers X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTDATA and X-KOBIL-ASTCLIENTID (omit the id when all zeros) into the URLRequest, and load that request. A plain request is refused (blank page).

After the WebView redirect: stop the navigation (decision handler false), send KSMSetAuthorisationCodeEvent with a completion handler and read the status of KSMSetAuthorisationCodeResultEvent there. Never print or log the authorisation code.
The reply of a request comes only through the request itself (completion handler, then, Future); never wait for it in a pushed-event handler.
A failed request shows in the status of its result event; a wrong event for the SDK state gives InvalidStateEvent.
A RuntimeErrorEvent is pushed and the SDK restarts itself afterwards: handle it right away, do not wait for the original result or the restart.

completion_handler.rule: Pass a completion handler for every event that has a result event; nil (or leaving it out) is allowed only for events whose result is none or Acknowledge, because their outcome arrives as pushed events at your delegate (or there is none). When unsure, pass a handler: it is always allowed.
completion_handler.source: API reference column "Result Event" (UI->MC rows), checked against every send in the GettingStarted Swift app: it passes no handler for exactly the events below and a handler for all others.
completion_handler.note: The GettingStarted still passes a handler for a few events the table lists as none (for example Login and Provide...ActivationCode...); a handler is never wrong.
completion_handler.lookup: sdk_event_result(event) gives the result event of every event the app sends and whether nil is allowed; check each event there.
